Samoa tsunami / building fragility

RiskScape functions tutorial · input checks, model switches and regional outputs

Local run notes   Figures generated 28 October 2026 · 7 plots
01 / INPUTS

Hazard and exposure

Inundation intensity is supplied as a raster; building footprints and constituencies provide the exposure and reporting geography. The tsunami hazard itself is calculated outside RiskScape.

MaxEnv_All_Scenarios_50m.tifHazard raster
Buildings_SE_Upolu.shpBuilding exposure
Samoa_constituencies.shpReporting areas
02 / CHECK

Exposure layer

The original QGIS inspection shows 6,260 features in the building layer. This is not the same quantity as the 2,059 buildings in the tutorial’s 50 m exposed-asset reference.

Worth checking: raster NoData handling, sampling method, and the geographic extent used to define exposure.
03 / MODEL

Consequence workflow

The engine samples event intensity at exposed assets, applies a consequence function, and aggregates outputs by constituency. Changing the function changes the question being asked, not the upstream hazard.

sample → hazard × buildings
compute → fragility / loss function
report → regional CSV + spatial output
04 / FUNCTIONS

DS1 / DS5 fragility

DS1 represents at least slight damage; DS5 corresponds to collapse. The curves below use the official function CSV values rather than estimated values from the stochastic run.

05 / EXPECTED VALUES

Regional expected consequences

Expected counts are sums of per-building damage probabilities, not observed damage counts. Regional differences reflect both exposure and fragility assumptions.

06 / REALIZATION

One stochastic collapse draw

A sampled outcome can differ from the corresponding expected count. One realization alone does not establish a confidence interval or quantify model uncertainty.

07 / NEXT CHECKS

Loose ends

Exposure sensitivity

Re-run with alternative raster sampling and footprint representations.

Curve transferability

Check whether material categories and DS thresholds are locally appropriate.

Random variation

Use fixed seeds and repeated draws before making uncertainty statements.

Reproducibility

Keep input hashes, run parameters, model version, and outputs together.
